rows.description: A friend faces bias and I want to shield him from everything. Wise: ask what he wants, support his voice instead of speaking over it. Harmful: making him feel helpless or turning it into my story.

rows.description: I catch myself assuming things about someone because of his religion or region. Wise: notice the thought without shame, test it against real individuals, and learn. Harmful: denying my own bias.

rows.description: Stopped at night by police, my heart pounds. Wise: stay calm, keep hands visible, be polite, carry ID, ask for the reason, and call someone; know that rights exist. Harmful: arguing or running.

rows.description: An officer asks me for money or presses me to sign a paper I have not read. Wise: do not sign what I do not understand, ask for a lawyer or a family member, and note names and numbers. Harmful: panicking and complying.
